title: AutomationContext: an explicit caller-provenance signal for flow params, replacing the headless-screen inference of PR #15787 (#15705 ruling ②)
body:
Filed by the triage seat (`session_01Tw7jnJinGHvoGSi8aFkhPJ`, seat post #6015) as the second half of the maintainer's ruling on #15705. The maintainer, reviewing `pm:on-hold` cards on 2026-09-23 in the triage session, answered 「15705同意」 to both pending items: ① a resume verb on the MCP tool surface, which stays on #15705 (`domain:cli`); ② this card.

Path: automation

## The ruling this card carries

Replace the inference in `service-automation`'s headless-screen verdict with an **explicit signal**: the doors that start a flow (the action door and the trigger door) say which keys in `params` the **caller** actually supplied, and the screen executor reads that signal instead of guessing.

## Why the inference has to go

PR #15787 (`b31ebfe7f`) lets a screen node continue without pausing when the caller already answered it. It decides "did the caller supply this field?" by inference (`callerSupplied` in `packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.ts`, read on `origin/main` `3ad89c1bcc`): the dispatcher seeds `params` with the record spread and the row id under several names, so the verdict has to rule those keys out one by one.

- **Four review passes on that PR each found a construction the previous pass had missed.** The dev's own reading (#15705, `5551189478`): "the signature of an inference that cannot be finished, not of a fix that is nearly done."
- **Two known constructions still SKIP a screen that should pause.** A skipped screen means a value the user was meant to enter is taken from the record instead. Both need a non-default `recordIdField` together with a `recordIdParam` naming a key the record lacks:
  - an object-less action whose record has a column literally named `recordId`;
  - an object-bound action whose record shadows both `recordId` and the `<object>Id` alias.
  - Both are documented in the PR body, the changeset and `flows.mdx` (#15705, `5552138777` and `5552406678`).
- Every new dispatcher seed reopens the question. That is how X1 happened in the first review.
- The durable-resume identity gap (#15812) is already closed by value comparison. This card removes the **class**, not another instance of it.

## Shape (⛔ not ruled beyond "explicit, not inferred")

- An additive, optional key on `AutomationContext` in `packages/spec`, filled by both doors. Precedent: `recordLoadDenied` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`), a producer signal that the door fills and the handler reads.
- The screen verdict reads the signal. When the signal is absent (an older producer), it keeps today's inference, whose failure direction is to pause.
- The implementing PR carries `needs:contract-review` (Clause-② yes: a published contract key is added).

## Acceptance

- Both boundary constructions above pause instead of skipping, each pinned on the real engine.
- Every existing pin in `screen-headless-satisfaction.test.ts` and `screen-headless-provenance-durable-resume.test.ts` stays green. Wherever a pin encodes the inference rather than the contract, the PR names it.
- The accepted-cost sentence in `flows.mdx` and the changeset is rewritten to describe the signal.

Refs: #15705 (the ruling) · PR #15787 · #15812 · #16370 (the same doors, caller-scope handling)

Dedupe: this is the ruled follow-up that #15705's report named as "open question B"; it has not been filed before (the dev and the PM seat both declined to file it without a ruling).
